events.title: Washington Resigns His Military Command
events.description: At the Maryland State House in Annapolis, George Washington gave up his commission as commander-in-chief of the Continental Army. He returned his authority to Congress and went home to Mount Vernon.
events.significance: By giving up power voluntarily, Washington set a lasting example of civilian control over the military in the new American republic.

events.title: "A Visit from St. Nicholas" Is Published
events.description: The poem now known as "The Night Before Christmas" appeared anonymously in a New York newspaper, the Troy Sentinel. It described a jolly, plump St. Nicholas arriving by sleigh with eight reindeer.
events.significance: The poem shaped the modern image of Santa Claus and became one of the most beloved Christmas traditions in the English-speaking world.

events.title: Van Gogh Cuts Off His Ear
events.description: After a breakdown in Arles, in the south of France, Vincent van Gogh severed part of his own left ear. This followed a heated dispute with his fellow painter Paul Gauguin.
events.significance: The episode became one of the most famous moments in art history. It marked the start of the painter's final, intensely productive period before his death in 1890.

events.title: The Federal Reserve Act Becomes Law
events.description: President Woodrow Wilson signed the Federal Reserve Act, creating the Federal Reserve System as the central banking system of the United States.
events.significance: The act gave the US a central bank to manage its money supply and respond to financial panics. The Federal Reserve remains one of the most powerful economic institutions in the world.
